title: Procurement & Boarding - SLA / DPA Escalation Review
summary: Redwood team walked Hearthline through outstanding MSA/DPA redlines, SLA tiers, KMS integration options, and pricing commit pathways. Customer raised data residency and subprocessor audit questions; legal requested DPA language for deletion and incident notification. Technical team wants a quick Dedicated pool pilot with SLO targets. Agreed to deliver redlined MSA, annotated DPA, and a Dedicated pilot proposal with cost/throughput estimates.
topics: Pricing approval workflows and egress fees
Pilot scope: Dedicated pool + smoke benchmarks
action_items: Maya Chen - send annotated MSA with suggested compromise language on liability cap and IP - due 2027-08-17
Liam Ortega - produce Dedicated pilot scope doc with expected p99 latency and cost estimates for 50k tokens/day - due 2027-08-19
Sofia Alvarez - share security pack (SOC2 report + DPA sample) and subprocessor list - due 2027-08-16
David Kim - provide list of non-negotiable DPA clauses and preferred incident SLA (window) - due 2027-08-20
next_steps: Redwood to circulate annotated MSA & DPA by EOD Monday
Customer to review pilot scope and confirm pilot start date (target week of 8/24)
Schedule legal-to-legal follow-up for redline agreement review (30 minutes)
Set up technical smoke test credentials for pilot (VPC peering / private endpoint)
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-08-12
Time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortega (Redwood SE), Sofia Alvarez (Redwood CSM), Nora Patel (Hearthline Procurement), David Kim (Hearthline Legal), Priya Singh (Hearthline Infosec), Markus Vogel (Hearthline Platform)

Summary: high level walkthrough and escalation on MSA/DPA points, SLA expectations, and pilot scoping.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. We're here to resolve the remaining MSA and DPA open items and get alignment on a Dedicated pilot for your workloads.
[00:18] Nora Patel: Thanks. To be clear, procurement wants to understand the approval path, sticky points and timing. Legal is obviously focused on the DPA subprocessors and deletion obligations.
[00:27] David Kim: Yeah, hi. We redlined the DPA and we'll send a consolidated list. The big ones are: audit access to subprocessors, tighter incident notification windows (we asked 24 hours), and explicit data deletion guarantees for customer data on both hot and cached storage.
[00:45] Liam Ortega: Understood. On the deletion note, we actually have prefix/KV cache behavior baked into our runtime — it can be configured to TTL or explicit delete on model request. We'll document the exact flow but just flag that there are multiple caches: application prefix cache, KV cache, and then disk-backed model artifacts.
[01:10] Priya Singh: When you say disk-backed artifacts, are those encrypted with a customer key or Redwood's key? We need KMS control.
[01:20] Markus Vogel: Also, data residency — can Dedicated be pinned to a single region with no egress? Our compliance team needs that.
[01:28] Maya Chen: Yes, Dedicated can be region-pinned. For KMS, we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations for Private deployments; for Dedicated we have an extended KMS option — we'll detail options in the security pack.
[01:46] David Kim: Great. On the DPA subprocessors, we can't accept unlimited chaining. We need a subprocessors list and a commitment to notify and provide audit summaries on changes.
[02:00] Sofia Alvarez: We'll attach the current subprocessor register — it's in the security pack — and we can commit to a notification window in the DPA appendix.
[02:10] Nora Patel: Pricing question — procurement noticed the egress fees and peak provisions. If we commit to a minimum monthly value for Dedicated, can we get a reduced egress schedule?
[02:21] Maya Chen: That's something we can do via reserved capacity discounts. Typically we map reserved commit to lower per-token pricing and reduced egress tiers for on-net traffic. We'll include a few tiered examples in the pilot proposal.
[02:33] David Kim: Liability cap — you're asking for company value cap and we pushed back. Legal wants to see a higher cap for regulated workloads. Is there room?
[02:42] Maya Chen: We can propose a middle ground in the MSA: carve-outs for data breach and will propose insurance-backed liability increases for enterprise customers. I'll send suggested language.
[02:52] Markus Vogel: From a technical standpoint, for the pilot we need to run p99 latency tests at 512 tokens and a throughput test of 5 concurrent requests. Can you guarantee warm-start behavior?
[03:05] Liam Ortega: We do support warm KV cache pins for Dedicated — you can preload KV state. For p99 we aim for <150ms on certain GPU profiles at that length, but it depends on model family and batch size. For the pilot we'll show realistic SLOs based on your expected prompt distribution.
[03:22] Priya Singh: Also need to confirm audit logging granularity — request traces, token-level cost, and whether logs contain prompt text or just hashes. For HIPAA-like workloads we can't have raw PII in logs.
[03:35] Sofia Alvarez: We have token-level cost and tracing. Logs can be redacted/per-route, and we can support prompt hashing or full-text logging on an opt-in basis for debug only. We'll include the options.
[03:50] David Kim: Incident response — you propose 72 hours SLA for incident acknowledgement, we asked 24. Can you commit to 24 for severity 1 incidents?
[04:00] Maya Chen: For Severity 1 we can commit to 1-hour acknowledgement, and then follow the remediation windows in the SLA appendix. For non-severity1 we usually do 24-72 depending on the case.
[04:12] Nora Patel: Procurement needs a clear sign-off matrix: who signs the MSA vs who signs SOW/purchase order. Also need timing for finance approval because reserved capacity impacts capex budgets across quarters.
[04:25] Maya Chen: We'll include a recommended sign-off flow and sample SOW template. For reserved capacity we usually do quarterly invoice and an option for annual commit at discount.
[04:37] Markus Vogel: Network connectivity — can we use VPC peering or private endpoint? We prefer no internet egress.
[04:45] Liam Ortega: We support VPC peering and Private endpoints. For the Dedicated pilot we can provision a private endpoint and coordinate the peering with your networking team. There may be one-time setup egress for images but runtime stays private.
[04:58] David Kim: About subprocessors again, if Redwood relies on a managed cloud GPU provider, will that be listed? We need to know if there's any subcontracting to low-trust regions.
[05:09] Sofia Alvarez: We have a bounded list of infrastructure subprocessors and we will highlight region constraints. We also have an option for on-prem appliance if that is required by your compliance.
[05:20] Nora Patel: Pricing approvals — timeline? If legal and procurement are aligned by end of next week can finance sign by the 22nd?
[05:28] Maya Chen: That's feasible. We'll aim to have the annotated MSA and pilot proposal in 3 business days so you can circulate.
[05:36] David Kim: One more technical question — KV cache persistence during failover: if you cold start across nodes how is TTL honored? We need guarantees for symmetrical behavior across zones.
[05:47] Liam Ortega: TTL is stored with the KV entries and honored at the runtime layer; cross-zone failover can rehydrate from persistent store, but there are edge cases for in-flight tokens. We'll document expected behavior and mitigation patterns like sticky routing.
[06:05] Nora Patel: Are there references or customers who've done a similar Dedicated pilot with healthcare data? We need a case for security review.
[06:14] Sofia Alvarez: We can share anonymized case studies and a healthcare checklist. We'll also provide a contact reference under NDA if required.
[06:25] David Kim: Let's set legal-to-legal next week to walk redlines. 30 minutes should be fine.
[06:32] Maya Chen: Sounds good. We'll send calendar invite.
[06:36] Markus Vogel: For the pilot, will you provide a test harness or do we deploy our own load generator?
[06:43] Liam Ortega: We'll provide a starter harness and scripts and can run an initial smoke test together.
[06:49] Nora Patel: Anything else from Redwood side?
[06:52] Maya Chen: We'll circulate the MSA annotations, DPA notes on subprocessors + incident windows, Dedicated pilot scope with costings, and the security pack.
[06:58] David Kim: We'll get David legal's redline list and team will review pilot doc.
[07:05] Maya Chen: Recap — action items and owners as per the note. We'll follow up with a legal-only invite and a technical kick-off once pilot scope is agreed. Appreciate everyone's time.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription fidelity: occasional mis-heard acronyms (e.g., KV cache transcribed as K V cache), speaker overlaps at 03:05 and 06:43 where crosstalk occurred. Some proper nouns (partner vendor names) omitted in audio capture.
